newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to launch new debate on working hours.
newsitem.headline: EU to launch new debate on working hours.

text.p: The European Commission is preparing to launch a debate next week on how to apply European Union rules on working hours and rest periods to truck drivers, sea fishermen, doctors in training and others who are now excluded.

A Commission official said the Commission was expected to issue a discussion paper on the EU's Working Time Directive, which limits the average work week to 48 hours, limits night shifts to an average of eight hours and says everyone should have four weeks paid leave a year and at least one day off a week.

The 1993 law was the subject last year of a controversial ruling by the European Court of Justice, which rejected Britain's argument that the rules had been adopted illegally as a health and safety measure.

The Commission has always been unhappy that the directive excluded more than nine million workers -- in the road, rail, inland waterways and air transport sectors, workers at sea and doctors in training.
But it delayed proposing that they be included until it had studied the court ruling.
The Commission declined to give details about the exact content of its planned "white paper", but the oil industry is already lobbying against applying the rules to offshore oil and gas operations.

The sector was originally excluded because of "the very special and often seasonal nature of the work, involving long helicopter flights, unique operational tasks and work patterns," the Oil Industry International Exploration and Production Forum said in a statement.
"These practices have evolved from decades of international experience and are very different from work on shore."
